movement_source: row 'Net interest margin (%)', column Full Year Ended 30 Jun 25 -> column Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26
headline: CBA's Group net interest margin fell 3 basis points to 2.05% in FY26 from 2.08% in FY25 (cash basis, continuing operations). The results book's walk attributes the decline to asset pricing (-5 bps, home lending down 4 bps and business/institutional lending down 1 bps on competition) and growth in liquid assets (-3 bps), partly offset by higher earnings on the replicating portfolio and capital hedges (+5 bps) and favourable portfolio mix (+2 bps). Excluding growth in liquid assets, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, the margin was stable. The results presentation corroborates the same -3 bps movement (2.08% to 2.05%) and the same key drivers.

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: Decreased margin by 5 basis points driven by home lending pricing (down 4 basis points) and business and institutional lending pricing (down 1 basis point), primarily reflecting the impact of competition. The results presentation corroborates: home loan competition (3), impact of cash rate lag (1), and business & Insto. lending (1).

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: Growth in liquid assets reduced margin by 3 basis points. The results presentation combines this with institutional repos at -4 bps total (increase in liquid assets -3, increase in institutional repos -1), noting +$15bn increase in average liquid assets and +$11bn increase in average institutional repos in FY26 vs FY25, with minimal impact on earnings.

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: Increased margin by 5 basis points driven by higher earnings on the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 4 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 1 basis point). The presentation labels this 'Interest rate risk hedging' at +5 bps (replicating portfolio +4, higher earnings on capital +1).

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by favourable asset mix from strong growth in business lending and favourable funding mix from strong growth in deposits. The presentation corroborates: favourable asset mix and deposits growing faster than lending.

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: Decreased margin by 2 basis points due to lower risk management income in Treasury and growth in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances. The presentation shows Treasury & Markets at -1 bps (a different split of the same total).

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: The bank states funding costs were flat, contributing 0 basis points to the margin movement.

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: The bank states basis risk was flat, contributing 0 basis points. This bar appears only in the results book walk; the presentation folds it into other bars.

disagreements.topic: Liquids vs Treasury & Markets bar split
values: Results presentation: Liquids & repos -4, Treasury & Markets -1
disagreements.explanation: The two documents group the same total -3 bps movement differently. The results book splits Liquids (-3) and Treasury & Markets (-2) separately, while the presentation combines Liquids & repos (-4) and shows Treasury & Markets at -1. Both sum to the same total. The results book is the primary framing per the walk preference rule.

values: Results presentation: no separate basis risk bar
disagreements.explanation: The results book shows a separate Basis risk bar at 0 bps; the presentation's walk does not include a basis risk bar, folding it into other bars. Both sum to the same total.

limitations: The two documents (results book page 28 and results presentation page 60) publish the same -3 bps FY25-to-FY26 NIM walk but group the bars differently: the book splits Liquids (-3) and Treasury & Markets (-2) separately, while the presentation combines Liquids & repos (-4) and shows Treasury & Markets at -1. I adopted the results book's framing as primary per the walk-preference rule; the presentation corroborates the total and the main drivers (asset pricing -5, funding 0, portfolio mix +2, capital/replicating +5).

The results presentation page 6 shows an 'Underlying net interest margin' of 2.04% (FY25) to 2.05% (FY26), a different (ex-liquids) measure from the headline NIM of 2.08% to 2.05% used for this task. This is a variant measure, not the headline row.

evidence_records.quote: [walk chart] NIM Movement since June 2025: Jun 25 Full Year 208 -> Jun 26 Full Year 205
Presented on a cash basis unless stated otherwise.

The Bank’s net interest margin decreased by 3 basis points on the prior year to 2.05%. Excluding growth in liquid assets, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, net interest margin was stable.

Asset pricing: Decreased margin by 5 basis points driven by home lending pricing (down 4 basis points) and business and institutional lending pricing (down 1 basis point), primarily reflecting the impact of competition.

numbers.label: Business and institutional lending pricing impact

evidence_records.quote: Portfolio mix: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by favourable asset mix from strong growth in business lending and favourable funding mix from strong growth in deposits.

Capital, Replicating and Other: Increased margin by 5 basis points driven by higher earnings on the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 4 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 1 basis point).

numbers.label: Capital, Replicating and Other NIM impact

evidence_records.quote: Treasury and Markets: Decreased margin by 2 basis points due to lower risk management income in Treasury and growth in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances.

Margins were broadly stable excluding growth in liquid assets and institutional reverse sale and repurchase agreements, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income. Underlying margins were supported by higher earnings on replicating portfolio and capital hedges, and the favourable mix impact of growth in business lending and deposits, largely offset by lower lending margins.
